retrieval.label: Engineering settings for an offline pipeline check. They are not the approved scientific protocol.
retrieval.scope: one index per document, built from every declared page; a question searches only its own document
retrieval.embedding: signed feature hashing of blake2b token digests, L2-normalised, no model download

chunking.pages_without_text: empty or missing OCR gives no chunk and is counted in ocr_condition
chunking.units: a CJK character (Han, Hiragana, Katakana) is one unit of weight 1; any other run of non-space characters is one unit of weight 2
chunking.window: chunk_size_words * 2 weight, so a chunk holds at most 360 CJK characters or 180 other words; the window advances by (chunk_size_words - chunk_overlap_words) words on the same scale
chunking.chunk_text: the page text of the span, each run of whitespace replaced by one space
chunking.without_cjk: text with no CJK character gets the boundaries and the chunk text of whitespace-words-v1

tokenisation.definition: NFKC, casefold, delete whitespace between CJK characters, then runs of Unicode letters or digits plus % and $ as word tokens and overlapping character bigrams for each CJK run
tokenisation.applied_to: chunk text and query text alike, for BM25 and for the hashing embedder
tokenisation.normalisation: Unicode NFKC, then casefold (the Unicode data version is in environment.unicodedata)
tokenisation.word_tokens: runs of Unicode letters or digits plus % and $, so 12% and $5 stay whole; _ and other symbols separate tokens
tokenisation.han_script: a run of Han, Hiragana or Katakana characters becomes overlapping character bigrams (one character gives itself); whitespace between two such characters is deleted first; no dictionary and no model
tokenisation.ascii_text: pure ASCII text gets the same tokens as ascii-alnum-v1
tokenisation.limits: a token count above zero says the question can be indexed, not that retrieval finds its evidence; bigrams of common Chinese function words count as tokens; Hangul is not segmented within a space-delimited word and Thai, Lao and Khmer are not segmented

ranking.fusion: 0.45 * min-max dense + 0.35 * min-max bm25 + 0.20 * reciprocal-rank component (k=60)
ranking.dense_note: faiss returns the dense scores of the top_k chunks only; other chunks enter the fusion with a dense score of 0
ranking.tie_breaking: numpy stable argsort: equal scores keep chunk order (page_idx ascending, then chunk_index)

no_evidence_reasons.no_text_chunks: every declared page has empty or missing OCR, so the document has zero chunks (an OCR condition)
no_evidence_reasons.no_text_content: the noisy text is non-empty but no chunk holds a letter or digit in any script (Unicode categories L and N), for example only Markdown heading markers. The input holds no usable evidence text. This is not missing OCR: the manifest records the page as ok because its text is non-empty
no_evidence_reasons.no_retrieval_tokens: chunks hold letters or digits but the multilingual-v1 tokeniser yields no token for any of them, so BM25 cannot index the document (rank_bm25 divides by zero). This is a limitation of the engineering tokeniser, not an OCR condition. Only stand-alone Arabic diacritic letters (U+FC5E to U+FC63 and U+FE70 to U+FE7E) reach it, because NFKC turns each into a space and a combining mark. The document is listed in generation_summary.json

retrieval.evidence_limit: at most top_k hits per question, all saved in predictions.jsonl with their scores
